 Trump administration Trump to hold one-on-one with Putin on the sidelines of Asia summit
 A U.S. official confirmed that the two leaders would hold a bilateral meeting despite White House officials indicating last week that Trump and Putin would not meet one-on-one. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Trump in Anchorage, Alaska, in 2025. Andrew Harnik / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 10:39 AM EST  /  Updated   Nov. 18, 2026, 11:08 AM EST By Monica Alba and Megan Brand President Donald Trump will hold a one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, a U.S. official confirmed, marking the leaders’ first in-person meeting in over a year. 
 The bilateral meeting was not initially on Trump’s schedule for his Asia trip. The president was already scheduled to hold a trilateral meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, where the leaders plan to discuss nuclear disarmament, the Iran war, trade and, Trump said Monday, Russia’s war with Ukraine. 
 The Kremlin had said ahead of the U.S.’ confirmation that the two leaders would be meeting one-on-one.

 Slide 1 of 1 The White House has not released information about the agenda for the bilateral meeting, which comes as major attacks continue in the Ukraine war with no end in sight. Trump’s meetings with the leaders of China and Russia — both U.S. adversaries — marks his administration’s continued shift away from traditional alliances and unconventional approach to diplomacy.
 A senior U.S. official previously told reporters that while the president intended to discuss Iran with Xi and Putin during their trilateral meeting, he did not plan to focus on the war in Ukraine. The official said last week that “it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there” with China.

 Slide 1 of 1 Trump and Putin previously met face-to-face in Alaska in August 2025. That summit ended without an agreement to end the war in Ukraine, something Trump has been pursuing since he began his second term. 
 Trump continued to express optimism about ending the war after the in-person meeting in Alaska did not lead to any ceasefire or breakthrough.
 Russia has continued to strike Ukraine, and vice versa, in the lead up to the meetings in Asia.
